{ "item": { "id": "062cc815-2b65-45b1-b36c-6ea67dfd1a0c", "content_type": "generic", "workflow_state": "public", "page_title": "Handling errors & retries", "short_description": "How Godzilla retries failed events, when they're dead-lettered, and how to replay them.", "body": "

Handling errors & retries

Every event that fails a transform or a destination write is retried automatically. This guide covers how that works and what to do when retries run out.

Automatic retries

Failed events retry with exponential backoff — 1s, 2s, 4s, up to a per-pipeline configurable ceiling. Most transient failures (a destination hiccup, a rate-limited third party) resolve within the first few attempts.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=pipeline-retry-config.json|language=json|code={ "retry_policy": { "max_attempts": 5, "backoff": "exponential", "initial_delay_ms": 1000 } }}}

Dead-lettering

An event that exhausts its retries is moved to that pipeline's dead-letter queue rather than dropped silently.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=Dead-lettered events don't retry themselves|body_html=

Once in the dead-letter queue, an event stays there until you replay it or explicitly discard it — it will not retry again on its own.

}}

Replaying events

Use the Events endpoint's replay action to re-run a specific dead-lettered event once the underlying issue is fixed.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=replay.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/events/evt_8f2c1a90/replay \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY"}}

Watching for failures

Subscribe to pipeline.failed via Webhooks so you find out about dead-lettered events before a customer does. See also Monitoring & alerts.

{{ds:component/docs-pagination|prev_href={{cms:item/3448ffab-598c-46e7-bda6-e7cdc4a1e7c6}}|prev_label=Connecting a data source|next_href={{cms:item/dc9f1302-e173-4034-9581-d06efea7d090}}|next_label=Scheduling & triggers}}", "version_token": "28b32bfd-c5c0-4f68-abd2-948e70c8a38d", "created_at": "2026-08-20T14:12:40.183Z", "updated_at": "2026-08-20T15:07:12.082Z", "placement_id": "0b6c15be-6394-4b2e-80ca-660125cbee7b", "folder_id": "c3e0ba4a-a491-4265-9848-556d298e6b6b", "file_name": "handling-errors-and-retries" } }

content.text: Now I'll create the new guide page:

input.short_description: Reshape, filter, and enrich events as they pass through a pipeline.
input.body:
Transforming events in flight

Once events enter your pipeline, you can reshape them, filter out unwanted records, or add enrichment data from external sources — all before they reach their destination.

Reshaping events

Use a transform to extract, rename, or restructure fields from incoming events. Transforms are JavaScript functions that receive an event and return a modified version of it.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=transform.js|language=javascript|code=export default function transform(event) { return { user_id: event.customer_id, name: event.first_name + ' ' + event.last_name, email: event.contact_email, created_at: new Date(event.signup_timestamp).toISOString() }; }}}

Return null from a transform to drop an event entirely, or throw an error to send it to the dead-letter queue.

Filtering events

Add a filter condition to your transform to block unwanted records at the source. A filter that returns false discards the event; true passes it through.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=filter.js|language=javascript|code=export default function filter(event) { // Only pass through events from paying customers return event.plan_type !== 'free'; }}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Filters are fast|body_html=

Filtering in the pipeline is cheaper than transforming and sending to a destination, then filtering downstream. Apply filters early.

}}

Enriching with external data

Your transform can call out to external APIs or databases to add data to each event. Be mindful of rate limits and latency — every enrichment call adds milliseconds to pipeline throughput.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=enrich.js|language=javascript|code=export default async function enrich(event) { const response = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/users/${event.user_id}`); const userData = await response.json(); return { ...event, user_tier: userData.tier, account_balance: userData.balance }; }}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=warning|title=Async transforms add latency|body_html=

Each external call blocks the pipeline for that event. Use with caution on high-throughput pipelines or consider batching lookups with a scheduled task instead.

}}

Chaining transforms

A single transform stage can run multiple functions in sequence. The output of one becomes the input to the next.

Monitoring transform failures

If a transform throws, the event is retried according to your retry policy. Watch transform error rates in Monitoring & alerts.

{{ds:component/docs-pagination|prev_href={{cms:item/3448ffab-598c-46e7-bda6-e7cdc4a1e7c6}}|prev_label=Connecting a data source|next_href={{cms:item/062cc815-2b65-45b1-b36c-6ea67dfd1a0c}}|next_label=Handling errors & retries}}

input.body:
Handling errors & retries

Every event that fails a transform or a destination write is retried automatically. This guide covers how that works and what to do when retries run out.

Automatic retries

Failed events retry with exponential backoff — 1s, 2s, 4s, up to a per-pipeline configurable ceiling. Most transient failures (a destination hiccup, a rate-limited third party) resolve within the first few attempts.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=pipeline-retry-config.json|language=json|code={ \"retry_policy\": { \"max_attempts\": 5, \"backoff\": \"exponential\", \"initial_delay_ms\": 1000 } }}}

Dead-lettering

An event that exhausts its retries is moved to that pipeline's dead-letter queue rather than dropped silently.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=Dead-lettered events don't retry themselves|body_html=

Once in the dead-letter queue, an event stays there until you replay it or explicitly discard it — it will not retry again on its own.

}}

Replaying events

Use the Events endpoint's replay action to re-run a specific dead-lettered event once the underlying issue is fixed.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=replay.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/events/evt_8f2c1a90/replay \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY\"}}

Watching for failures

Subscribe to pipeline.failed via Webhooks so you find out about dead-lettered events before a customer does. See also Monitoring & alerts.

{{ds:component/docs-pagination|prev_href={{cms:item/00ae9a4e-7788-4e8e-906a-f65b23820ba2}}|prev_label=Transforming events in flight|next_href={{cms:item/dc9f1302-e173-4034-9581-d06efea7d090}}|next_label=Scheduling & triggers}}
